Which integral gives the area of the finite region bounded by $y=2{x}^{2}-2$ and $y=1-{x}^{2},$ shown above?

*(Note: Figure not drawn to scale)*
question.worked_solution:
The diagram shows that the intersection points between the two graphs occur when $x=-1$ and $x=1.$ So these will be our limits of integration.

To determine which is the lower function and which is the upper, let's draw our vertical arrow.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14273827/assets/c6390f35fb796517054a15f16ee12f1354fa04f315f3cf1d91d498f19e73e15b.png)

The vertical line 

- *enters* the region through the lower function $y=2{x}^{2}-2,$ and

- *leaves* through the upper function $y=1-{x}^{2}.$

Therefore, the integral that gives our area is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}[\,(\text{upper function})-(\text{lower function})\,]\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}[\,(1-{x}^{2})-(2{x}^{2}-2)\,]\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}(-3{x}^{2}+3)\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$
